title: Spengler wins the Hockenheim finale and the DTM title by four points
dek: Bruno Spengler won the Hockenheim finale from third on the grid, 2.214 seconds ahead of Gary Paffett, to take the DTM title by four points as BMW also won the team and manufacturers' crowns.

chapters.title: Three points and one race
text: The tenth and last race of the 2012 DTM season, at the Hockenheimring on Sunday 21 October, still had three drivers who could win the title. Gary Paffett, who had led the standings since the first round, arrived on 127 points, three ahead of Bruno Spengler on 124. Jamie Green was third on 109, 18 back, so he needed a victory and for both rivals to finish well down the order. Mike Rockenfeller, on 85, was out of reach even with a win.

The run-in had turned on Valencia three weeks earlier. Augusto Farfus had won there from pole for BMW Team RBM, Paffett had retired with damage and scored nothing, and Spengler had come through from 12th on the grid despite a drive-through penalty to finish sixth and cut an 11-point deficit to three. Over the previous five races a lead of 40 points had been whittled down to that margin.

There was a personal edge for Spengler, who had driven for Mercedes from his DTM debut in 2005 until the end of 2011 before moving to BMW for the marque's return. Mercedes motorsport chief Norbert Haug pointed out that Spengler had not been able to win the title in five attempts with them. It was also the last DTM race for David Coulthard, who had announced that he would stop after three seasons, and for Susie Wolff.

chapters.title: Farfus on pole again, with the title rivals behind
text: Farfus took pole for the second race in a row. The BMW Team RBM rookie set 1:34.140 in the final session, 0.121 seconds faster than Paffett's 1:34.261, with Spengler third on 1:34.268, only 0.007 slower than the Mercedes. Mattias Ekström was fourth for Abt Sportsline on 1:34.627, which made the final part of qualifying a four-way fight, and the two championship rivals were set to start on the grid's first two rows.

Behind them Joey Hand, Martin Tomczyk and Dirk Werner started fifth, sixth and seventh, so five BMW M3s were in the top seven. Edoardo Mortara was eighth for Rosberg and Green ninth, ahead of Filipe Albuquerque, Rockenfeller and Christian Vietoris. Andy Priaulx was 13th. Timo Scheider, who had set the eighth-fastest time, was placed 22nd and last on the grid, and Coulthard and Wolff started 20th and 21st.

Farfus said he had not expected pole and would have been happy with a top five, since the car had been hard to drive on Friday. The team changed it during qualifying and it came good when it mattered. Spengler praised the work of BMW Team Schnitzer and said the final race would be a real showdown.

chapters.title: Spengler takes the lead on lap one
text: Farfus led away from pole but did not stay there. Paffett's rear wheels spun at the start and he lost places, while Spengler got away well from third, passed the Mercedes and had taken the lead from Farfus by the end of the first lap. Ekström and Hand ran wide together at the Spitzkehre while fighting for position, and that gave Paffett third place back. After six laps Spengler led from Farfus and Paffett.

The Audis suffered early. Adrien Tambay's race ended on the first lap after a collision, and Rockenfeller was gone after two laps. Green made up places in the opening stint and passed Hand for fifth around lap ten.

chapters.title: Paffett jumps Farfus in the pits
text: The first stops came on lap 11, when Farfus and Paffett came in together. The Mercedes crew turned Paffett round quickly and the two cars left the pit lane side by side, with Paffett getting ahead on the exit to take second place. Spengler, who kept the lead through both rounds of stops, later credited Schnitzer's pit work.

The pits also ended several races. Ekström's Audi stopped after eleven laps with a problem on its front-right wheel following his stop, and Robert Wickens parked his Mercedes in the pits on lap 20. On lap 23 Scheider hit Coulthard's Mercedes and spun it, and Coulthard went into the pits the following lap to end his DTM career. Scheider was given a drive-through penalty. Miguel Molina then ran into the gravel at the Sachs Kurve at around mid-distance.

chapters.title: Paffett closes to 1.3 seconds
text: After the second stops Paffett began to eat into the lead. Spengler's advantage of about 4.1 seconds fell to roughly 2.0 within five laps, and with ten laps to go it was down to 1.3 seconds. Paffett was warned for putting all four wheels off the track at the first corner on lap 34, and from then on he had to keep within the limits or risk a penalty.
The gap then held. In mid-field Mortara, Priaulx, Hand and Ralf Schumacher were all within two seconds of each other as they fought for sixth place, while Green and Werner ran in fourth and fifth.

chapters.title: Spengler holds on by 2.214 seconds
text: Spengler took the flag after 42 laps in 1:07:59.069, 2.214 seconds ahead of Paffett, and so beat him to the title by four points. Farfus completed the podium in third, 11.954 seconds behind the winner after starting from pole. Green was fourth, 23.479 seconds back, having climbed from ninth on the grid, and Werner took fifth for Schnitzer, in front of Mortara and Priaulx.

Hand was eighth, Schumacher ninth and Vietoris tenth, which meant five BMWs finished in the top eight. Paffett set the fastest lap, a 1:35.402 on lap 29. Wolff finished 13th in her last DTM race, while Tomczyk was 14th, a lap down.

chapters.title: BMW completes a triple in its comeback year
text: Spengler finished the year on 149 points, four ahead of Paffett on 145, with Green third on 121. It was his fourth win of 2012, after the Lausitzring, the Nürburgring and Oschersleben, and his first DTM title. He said he had spent a lot of time looking in the rear-view mirror in the closing laps, with Paffett steadily closing, but had been able to keep his pace and finish the job. Had the top two places been reversed, Paffett would have won the title by ten points, 152 to 142.

For Paffett it was a hard way to lose. He had led the standings from the first round to the final race, and scored points in nine of the ten races. He said that he felt his team had deserved to win the championship title just as much as Spengler and BMW, and congratulated the new champion. Green's third place was his best championship finish, and he had scored in every one of the ten races. Mercedes' Norbert Haug said a four-point deficit was no reason to be sad and promised a stronger start to 2013.

BMW took all three titles in its comeback season. BMW Team Schnitzer won the team classification and BMW won the manufacturers' championship, with five of its six cars in the points: Spengler won, Farfus was third, Werner fifth, Priaulx seventh and Hand eighth. BMW motorsport director Jens Marquardt said the marque had come back after almost 20 years wanting to be competitive quickly, and Schnitzer team principal Charly Lamm put the title down to Spengler's nerves and perfect pit stops. Team RBM's Bart Mampaey, whose cars finished third and seventh, said the team had played an important part in how the race unfolded. Rockenfeller finished fourth in the drivers' standings on 85 points, ahead of Mortara on 82 and Ekström on 81.

It was also a day of farewells. Coulthard ended his three seasons in the DTM with a spin and an early retirement, and Wolff finished 13th in her last race in the series. The season, the first under the DTM's new regulations, was over.

facts.v: Bruno Spengler won the 42-lap race in 1:07:59.069, 2.214 seconds ahead of Gary Paffett, and finished the season on 149 points to Paffett's 145.
